recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is for FHIR-14220. Any future adjustment to the broader answerOption/answerValueSet type model should be handled under later issues such as FHIR-40780, not this STU3 invariant fix.
issue_request: FHIR-14220 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 FHIR-core Questionnaire issue asking to modify invariant que-5 because the option property effectively allowed only valueCoding and blocked integer, date, time, and string option values.
initial_application: Jira comments record application as svn revision 13258. No FHIR-14220-labelled git commit was found in the current repository history, but the imported git source before FHIR-20396 already had que-5 allowing choice/open-choice plus decimal, integer, date, dateTime, time, string, and quantity, and answerOption.value[x] included integer, date, time, string, Coding, and Reference.
additional_context: FHIR-20396 later removed choice/open-choice item.type codes and introduced answerConstraint/Coding-oriented wording. FHIR-40780 later aligned que-5 with answerOption.value[x], limited que-5 to answerOption, added que-5b for answerValueSet, and added a type-matching invariant. The linked Questionnaire Zulip thread confirms answerOption was intentionally broadened while answerValueSet was tightened.
reconciliation: No source change was made. source/fhir.ini actively includes Questionnaire, and current source/questionnaire/structuredefinition-Questionnaire.xml already allows coding, decimal, integer, date, dateTime, time, string, quantity, reference, and uri items to have answerOption, with corresponding answerOption.value[x] choices.

related_jiras.note: Removed choice/open-choice from Questionnaire.item.type and reframed option-list behavior through answerConstraint, changing how the old STU3 wording maps to current source.
Aligned que-5, answerOption.value[x], answerValueSet restrictions, and type-matching rules in the current Questionnaire source.
Corrected answerOption definition wording after answerOption types had been opened beyond choice/open-choice.
